title: Handmade Chandelier Assembly: Hook Forging, Arm Forming, Soldering, and Antique Brass Finish

locations.name: Fabrication department (shop)
locations.basis: explicit mention in transcript: 'Here we are in the fabrication department'

summary: This Old House follows a homeowner through a shop that handcrafts chandeliers and other fixtures. The episode centers on a custom eight-arm dining-room chandelier, detailing sequence—from initial design notes and parts overview to the actual fabrication steps (hook forging, arm forming, and soldering bobeche), through a multi-step finish (cleaning, acid etch, color application) and final electrical wiring. The piece is described as handmade-to-order with a living antique-brass finish, and the team notes a roughly three-week turnaround. The segment emphasizes craftsmanship, consistency across arms, and the integration of the fixture with home hardware and patina over time.

sections.title: Shop tour and fixture introduction
sections.description: Host and homeowner Helen tour a shop that makes lanterns and chandeliers by hand, discussing finishes and sample options ahead of selecting a dining-room chandelier.

sections.title: Chandelier parts overview
sections.description: Demonstrates the chandelier's core components and notes how the parts fit together, including the decorative wire-wrapped stem and bottom curl that end in a hook.

sections.title: Decorative hook fabrication
sections.description: First step: building the decorative hook by hammering the end flat and then rolling it in a roller to form the hook shape.

sections.title: Arm formation and patterning
sections.description: Arms are formed by hand, with the bottom curl bent around a circle and matched to a pattern to ensure even, consistent arms; the chandelier has eight arms.

sections.title: Soldering bobeche to arms
sections.description: Hands-on soldering of bobeches to each arm, with a note on four factors for a perfect joint (flux, solder, heat, and experience) and a cooling test using water.

sections.title: Joint finishing and quality check
sections.description: Observation of a finished solder joint with a bead; emphasis on achieving a solid, well-formed connection.

sections.title: Finishing process and color choice
sections.description: Parts move through a four-step finish: cleaning bath to remove residues, acid etch to prepare for color, application of a coloring agent, and final finish in dark antique brass described as a living finish that ages instead of lacquer coating.

sections.title: Wiring and final assembly
sections.description: Preview of wiring one fixture (white socket installation) and notes that each piece is made to order with a turnaround of about three weeks.

sections.title: Closing and call to action
sections.description: Host thanks viewers and invites them to explore This Old House videos and subscribe for new content.
